transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me?

I guess the main thing is… I keep running into a wall with work that takes real mental effort. Like monthly reports, or planning a multi-site health event. I know it’s important, but I just keep putting it off, and it’s starting to be a problem.
Has this trouble with procrastinating on effortful mental tasks been something you've dealt with since childhood or your school years, or is this a newer pattern that started more recently?

It’s been around a long time, I think. Even in elementary school, teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but I’d be daydreaming or losing worksheets. Homework was a problem too—I’d forget to turn it in unless my mom checked my backpack every night.
When you put off these tasks, is it more because you worry you won't do them perfectly or exactly right, or is it more that you find it hard to focus and organize yourself to start them?

More the second one. It’s not really about perfect… I just have a hard time getting myself focused and organized enough to start. Anything that takes sitting-down brain work, like reports or event planning, I kind of hit a wall and put it off, even when I know it matters.
Growing up and now, have you also noticed things like feeling restless, fidgety, interrupting others, or acting impulsively, or has it mainly been the focus and organization difficulties?

Mostly it’s the focus and organizing. Like when I’m juggling work projects, committee stuff, outreach events… I’ll have notes in three different places and I can’t really sort out what needs to happen first. Then I end up rushing at the end.

Would you say these focus and organization struggles are causing real problems not just at work, but also in other areas of your life—like at home, in relationships, or managing personal responsibilities?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still getting by, mostly. Work and community stuff haven’t fallen apart or anything. But there have been gaps people had to cover for me, and some deadlines have slipped.

And outside work… I’ve had to make those awkward last-minute apologies to coworkers or friends when I didn’t follow through like I said I would. It’s embarrassing.
Have you been feeling persistently sad, anxious, or low in energy during this time, or is your mood generally okay aside from the frustration with these tasks?
I don’t think it’s been that, no. My mood is… mostly okay, I guess. I get frustrated with myself when I’m behind, but I wouldn’t say I’m persistently sad or anything like that.
Do you notice yourself feeling persistently worried, tense, or on edge in a way that makes it hard to concentrate, separate from the frustration you feel about unfinished tasks?
Not really… I don’t think I’m walking around tense or on edge all the time. It’s more that I get annoyed when things pile up and I’m behind.
Have you noticed any issues with your sleep quality, or do you regularly use alcohol, cannabis, or other substances that might be affecting your concentration?
I haven’t really noticed anything obvious there. Sleep is… okay, I think. And I’m not regularly using anything like that, at least not in a way I’d think is affecting my focus.
Do you often find yourself losing important items like keys or your phone, or forgetting appointments and commitments in your daily life?

Yeah… I do forget things. Not so much losing my phone or keys, but I’ll forget to return calls, like from volunteers, or miss little errands for events. A couple times a community meeting just completely slipped my mind until someone texted me, and then I had to apologize.
Do you find that you're easily distracted by things going on around you—like noises, conversations, or unrelated thoughts—when you're trying to focus on a task?

Yeah… that happens. Like in meetings, I’ll be trying to follow a budget update, and then a phone buzzing or people talking out in the hall pulls me off. Sometimes it’s not even noise—just a thought about something I forgot for the league—and then I realize I missed the next few minutes.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a lifelong (since elementary school) pattern of inattention—difficulty sustaining focus on effortful mental tasks, disorganization, forgetfulness, distractibility by external stimuli and internal thoughts, and losing track of tasks/appointments. These symptoms are pervasive across work and personal/community domains, causing functional impairment (missed deadlines, need for others to cover tasks, repeated apologies for follow-through failures). No significant hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (restlessness, interrupting, impulsivity) are endorsed, consistent with a predominantly inattentive presentation. Mood symptoms (persistent sadness, low energy) and anxiety symptoms (chronic worry, tension) are explicitly denied, and no substance use or sleep disturbance is present to better explain the concentration difficulties, effectively ruling out depressive or anxiety disorders as primary causes. The chronicity since childhood, cross-situational impairment, and predominance of inattentive symptoms support a diagnosis of ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation (F90.0).
